why-it-exists explains the 2017-era buckets, the fingerprinting risk of rare low values, the high-end segmentation demand (w3c/device-memory#50, on-device AI), and the spec change making bounds implementation-defined. Migration advice (threshold comparisons, never value allowlists) is derived directly from those incidents.

First mobile pass caught the 6-column compat tables crushing to one character per line at 360px; fixed with .compat-table{min-width} so they scroll inside .table-wrap. guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and overflow containers instead of fixed widths; use overflow-wrap on unbreakable tokens; give replaced elements like iframe a block display value rather than clipping with overflow:hidden; use flex-wrap for wrapping rows.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells; <wbr> inserted in the long child-page H1s (navigator.deviceMemory, Sec-CH-Device-Memory); the showcase iframe is display:block with max-width:100%; baseline-browsers list uses flex-wrap. Removed revision 1's table-layout:fixed in favour of the exemplar's intrinsic sizing, and added .compat-table{min-width:36-44rem} after the mobile matrix pass showed the 5-6 column compat tables crushing at 360px - they now scroll inside .table-wrap instead.

guidanceConsulted.query: lazy loading embedded iframe demo accessibility title
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Place content in landmarks, keep a sequential heading outline, use semantic tables with caption/scope, and give embedded/media content accessible names.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: single main landmark per page, sequential h1>h2>h3, th scope=row/col on all doc-tables, the live-demo iframe carries a descriptive title attribute and loading=lazy, and the baseline banner is role=note with an aria-label. Exception: no <caption> elements - the tables are immediately preceded by their section headings, matching the accepted exemplar pattern across the site.
